claims.source: Inhibition of proliferation with either mitomycin C or aphidicolin did not affect cell migration speeds in either the rounded or elongated areas (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claims.claim: Blocking proliferation slightly reduces track straightness and increases the track displacement angle.
claims.source: However, blocking proliferation slightly reduced track straightness, implying a reduction in persistence (Figure 1—figure supplement 3F) and increased the track displacement angle (Figure 1—figure supplement 3G).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3F and 3G.

claims.claim: Re-embedded aggregates lose laminin V expression over time.
claims.source: Consistent with the change in matrix environment associated with the transplantation process, re-embedded aggregates lost laminin V expression over time (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: Aggregates express fibronectin throughout the experiments without any evident regional differences in the elongating areas.
claims.source: They expressed fibronectin throughout the experiments without any evident regional differences in the elongating areas of aggregates (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Collagen 1 condenses around aggregates that have begun to elongate, forming dense bands that extend away from the cells into the gel.
claims.source: Aggregate elongation appeared to coincide with change in fibril organization. Whereas fibrils appeared isotropic in acellular gels, collagen condensed around the aggregates that had begun to elongate, forming dense bands that extended away from the cells into the gel.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on observations of collagen organization using CNA35 labeling.

claims.claim: Collagen coherency increases with the increase in symmetry ratio after 8 days culture.
claims.source: Then, we compared collagen coherency with aggregate shape, as measured by the symmetry ratio (Figure 2B), after 8 days culture, when elongation was established. Overall, collagen coherency increased with the increase in symmetry ratio (Figure 2C), implying that the degree of collagen bundling increased with aggregate elongation.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Collagen coherency is greater in regions proximate to the elongating parts of aggregates compared with the non-elongating parts.
claims.source: Furthermore, closer examination around elongating aggregates showed that collagen coherency was greater in regions proximate to the elongating parts of the aggregates compared with the non-elongating parts (Figure 2D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: Aggregates that remain spherical show no regional differences in collagen organization.
claims.source: In contrast, aggregates that remained spherical showed no regional differences in collagen organization.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on analysis of collagen coherency around non-elongated aggregates.

claims.claim: Collagen 1 coherency increases around elongating areas as aggregates break symmetry in the first three days of culture.
claims.source: Because aggregates varied in the timing of when they broke symmetry, we examined aggregates by live imaging in the first three days of the assays. We then subdivided these based on their symmetry ratio and compared the coherency of collagen 1 around the elongating areas of aggregates with that around the non-elongating areas (i.e., those that remained rounded, expressed as a fold difference). This showed that collagen 1 coherency increased around the elongating areas as they broke symmetry (Figure 2E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: Collagen bundling requires cell proliferation, as coherency is reduced by treatment with mitomycin C or aphidicolin.
claims.source: Collagen bundling required cell proliferation, as coherency was reduced by treatment with either mitomycin C or aphidicolin (Figure 2F and G).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2F and G.

claims.claim: Collagen bundling is reduced when cellular contractility is inhibited with blebbistatin or Y27632.
claims.source: Collagen bundling was also reduced when we inhibited cellular contractility with the myosin antagonist, blebbistatin, or the Rho kinase (ROCK) inhibitor, Y27632 (Figure 2H, I), consistent with reports that cell contractility can condense collagen (Brownfield et al., 2013; Buchmann et al., 2021; Gjorevski et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2H and I, and citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: Collagen condensation persists around aggregates treated with NSC23766, which does not affect aggregate elongation or cell movement speed.
claims.source: In contrast, collagen condensation persisted around aggregates treated with the Rac1 GEF inhibitor NSC23766, which did not affect aggregate elongation or the speed with which cells moved within the aggregates (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: The collagen gel around non-elongating areas of aggregates shows a broad distribution of orientations relative to the axis of the aggregate.
claims.source: First, we assembled histograms of gel orientation, setting the principal axis of elongation in the whole aggregate as 0o (Figure 2J). The gels around non-elongating areas of the aggregates showed a broad distribution of orientations relative to the axis of the aggregate (Figure 2J).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2J.

claims.claim: The gel around elongating regions of aggregates tends to orient with the principal axis of the aggregates.
claims.source: In contrast, the gel around the elongating regions of aggregates tended to orient with the principal axis of the aggregates.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on analysis of gel orientation shown in Figure 2J.

claims.claim: The angle difference between the axes of collagen polarity and aggregate elongation is significantly smaller around elongating regions than around non-elongating regions.
claims.source: We found that the angle differences between the axes of collagen polarity and aggregate elongation was significantly smaller around the elongating regions than around the non-elongating regions of the aggregates (Figure 2K).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2K.

claims.claim: Collagen fibers become isotropically distributed in unstretched gels and become more coherent and polarized immediately after stretching.
claims.source: Second harmonic imaging confirmed that collagen fibers were isotropically distributed in the unstretched gels and became more coherent (bundled) and more polarized immediately after stretching (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D), with their principal axes oriented in the direction of stretch (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by second harmonic imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, D, and E.

claims.claim: Polarization of collagen fibrils can be preserved for at least 7 days after the application of stretch by re-embedding the collagen rings in a larger collagen gel.
claims.source: Moreover, polarization of the collagen fibrils could be preserved for at least 7 days after the application of stretch by re-embedding the collagen rings in a larger collagen gel (Figure 3A–C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A-C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: When gels are allowed to float in medium after stretching, gel coherency and polarity revert to that of unstretched gels.
claims.source: In contrast, when gels were allowed to float in medium after stretching (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), gel coherency (Figure 3E) and polarity (Figure 3F) reverted to that of unstretched gels.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3D, E, and F.

claims.claim: Aggregates do not become elongated during the period when stretch is actively applied.
claims.source: Interestingly, the aggregates did not become elongated during the period when stretch was actively applied. The symmetry ratios of aggregates immediately after stretching were identical to those in unstretched aggregates (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and B.

claims.claim: Symmetry breaking occurs earlier when stretched gels are allowed to retain collagen polarization by re-embedding (35.14 ± 3.28 hr) compared with aggregates in non-stretched gels (68.40 ± 5.88 hr).
claims.source: However, symmetry breaking occurred earlier when stretched gels were allowed to retain collagen polarization by re-embedding (35.14 ± 3.28 hr, Figure 3G and H) compared with aggregates that were allowed to break symmetry spontaneously in non-stretched gels (68.40 ± 5.88 hr, p<0.001).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3G and H.

claims.claim: The symmetry ratios of aggregates embedded in stretch-polarized gels are significantly greater than those seen with native gels.
claims.source: Moreover, the degree of elongation was also enhanced once it had begun. The symmetry ratios of aggregates embedded in stretch-polarized gels were significantly greater than those seen with native gels (Figure 3I).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3I.

claims.claim: Stretch-polarized aggregates elongate preferentially along the axis of the exogenous stretch, whereas aggregates in non-stretched gels elongate in a random direction.
claims.source: Stretch-polarized aggregates also elongated preferentially along the axis of the exogenous stretch, whereas aggregates in non-stretched gels elongated in a random direction (Figure 3G and J, Figure 3—figure supplement 2C and D, Video 2).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3G, J, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2C and D, and Video 2.

claims.claim: The angle difference between collagen fiber polarity and aggregate elongation is significantly smaller in stretch-polarized gels than in unstretched control gels.
claims.source: The angle difference between collagen fiber polarity and aggregate elongation was significantly smaller in stretch-polarized gels than in unstretched control gels (Figure 3K).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3K.

claims.claim: Collagen gel reorganization is preserved in stretch-polarized gels and is oriented in the direction of the original stretch.
claims.source: Of note, collagen gel reorganization was preserved in the stretch-polarized gels (Figure 3L and M), even in the presence of cellular aggregates, and this was oriented in the direction of the original stretch.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3L and M.

claims.claim: Similar intensity of fibronectin staining is seen in stretch-polarized aggregates compared with controls, suggesting that fibronectin deposition is not stimulated by stretch stimulation.
claims.source: In contrast, similar intensity of fibronectin staining was seen in stretch-polarized aggregates compared with controls, suggesting that fibronectin deposition was not stimulated by the stretch stimulation (Figure 3—figure supplement 2E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2E.

claims.claim: The proportion of aggregates that elongate after stretching is reduced when the gels are floated rather than being re-embedded.
claims.source: Importantly, the impact of stretch on the aggregates was disrupted when collagen polarization was reversed. The proportion of aggregates that elongated after stretching was reduced when the gels were floated rather than being re-embedded (Figure 4A) and their length of elongation was reduced (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4A and B.

claims.claim: Cell-based forces cannot overcome the external forces acting on the gel as the reversal of collagen polarization occurs even when aggregates are incorporated into the gel.
claims.source: Of note, cell-based forces could not overcome the external forces acting on the gel as the reversal of collagen polarization occurred even when aggregates were incorporated into the gel (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: Stretch polarization stimulates cell proliferation.
claims.source: Since cell proliferation was a major driver of spontaneous aggregate elongation, we then asked if it was altered when the collagen gel was polarized by stretch. Indeed, we found that stretch polarization stimulated cell proliferation (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: An increase in the proportion of Ki67-positive cells is evident at day 1 after stretch polarization, whereas it does not increase till day 2 in unstretched gels.
claims.source: An increase in the proportion of Ki67-positive cells was evident at day 1 after stretch polarization, whereas it did not increase till day 2 in unstretched gels.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on time-course data of Ki67 staining.

claims.claim: The proportion of Ki67 cells is consistently greater in stretch-polarized gels during the early phase of culture (days 1–3) as well as at the end of experiments (day 8).
claims.source: Moreover, the proportion of Ki67 cells was consistently greater in stretch-polarized gels during the early phase of culture (days 1–3) as well as at the end of our experiments (day 8).
claims.evidence: The claim is based on time-course data of Ki67 staining.

claims.claim: Cell proliferation mediates the enhanced elongation in stretched gels as both the length and symmetry ratio of stretch-stimulated aggregates are reduced by mitomycin C and aphidicolin.
claims.source: Cell proliferation mediated the enhanced elongation in the stretched gels as both the length (Figure 5B) and symmetry ratio (Figure 5C) of stretch-stimulated aggregates were reduced by mitomycin C and aphidicolin.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 5B and C.

claims.claim: Proliferation is not increased if gels are allowed to float, rather than being re-embedded, after stretching.
claims.source: However, proliferation was not increased if gels were allowed to float, rather than being re-embedded, after stretching. Floating the gels reduced the proportion of proliferating cells in the aggregates overall (Figure 5D and E) as well as those specifically within the area of elongation (Figure 5F), compared with gels that had been re-embedded to preserve collagen polarization.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 5D, E, and F.

claims.claim: The proportion of ERK-activated cells is significantly greater in the elongating regions of aggregates that had spontaneously broken symmetry than in the non-elongating areas.
claims.source: We found that the proportion of ERK-activated cells was significantly greater in the elongating regions of aggregates that had spontaneously broken symmetry than in the non-elongating areas (Figure 6A and B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data using ERK/KTR biosensor shown in Figure 6A and B.

claims.claim: ERK activation is especially apparent in cells at the surface of aggregates that are in contact with the collagen gel.
claims.source: This was especially apparent in cells at the surface of aggregates that were in contact with the collagen gel (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: No changes in nuclear Yap1 staining are detected that might indicate Hippo pathway activation in the experiments.
claims.source: In contrast, although Hippo pathway signaling has been implicated in breaking the symmetry of epithelial organoids (Serra et al., 2019), we did not detect any changes in nuclear Yap1 staining that might indicate that this pathway was being activated in our experiments (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B and C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B and C, and citation to Serra et al., 2019.

claims.claim: FR180204 reduces cell proliferation in response to stretch polarization.
claims.source: This notion was supported by finding that FR180204 (50 μM) reduced cell proliferation in response to stretch polarization (Figure 6D and E) and decreased the proportion of aggregates that elongated (Figure 6F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 6D, E, and F.

claims.claim: FR180204 reduces the length and asymmetric morphology of aggregates that do elongate.
claims.source: As well, the length (Figure 6G) and asymmetric morphology (Figure 6H) were reduced in those aggregates that did elongate.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 6G and H.

claims.claim: ERK1/2 is critical for collagen polarization to stimulate cell proliferation for aggregate elongation.
claims.source: Thus, ERK1/2 appeared to be critical for collagen polarization to stimulate cell proliferation for aggregate elongation.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental results showing that ERK inhibition blocks proliferation and elongation in response to collagen polarization.

claims.claim: MCF10A cells express α2β1-integrin.
claims.source: This class of integrins contains a number of collagen 1 receptors, including α2β1-integrin (Heino, 2000; Käpylä et al., 2000), which was expressed in our MCF10A cells (Figure 7B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 7B and citations to Heino, 2000 and Käpylä et al., 2000.

claims.claim: mAb AIIB2 blocks the induction of proliferation in stretch-polarized gels.
claims.source: mAb AIIB2 (15 μg/ml) was added as aggregates were transplanted into the collagen gel rings and replenished after 7 days. mAb AIIB2 blocked the induction of proliferation in stretch-polarized gels, the proportion of Ki67-positive cells being significantly reduced in AIIB2-treated cultures compared with controls (Figure 7C and D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 7C and D.

claims.claim: After 3 days incubation, 49.19% ± 1.61% aggregates start to elongate in controls, whereas less than 20% of aggregates elongate when β1-integrins are inhibited (17.86% ± 4.78%).
claims.source: After 3 days incubation, 49.19% ± 1.61% aggregates started to elongate in controls, whereas less than 20% of aggregates elongated when β1-integrins were inhibited (AIIB2: 17.86% ± 4.78%) (Figure 7E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 7E.

claims.claim: mAb AIIB2-treated aggregates that eventually elongate remain shorter and less asymmetric than in the absence of AIIB2.
claims.source: Moreover, even when mAb AIIB2-treated aggregates eventually elongated upon prolonged culture (comparing the proportion of elongated cells at 7 days with that at 3 days), these aggregates remained shorter (Figure 7F) and less asymmetric (Figure 7G) than in the absence of AIIB2.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 7F and G.

claims.claim: The ability of stretch polarization to stimulate ERK signaling at early (day 2) and later stages (day 7) is reduced when β1-integrins are blocked with mAb AIIB2.
claims.source: Finally, we asked if the ERK response required β1-integrins. Indeed, we found that the ability of stretch polarization to stimulate ERK signaling at early (day 2) and later stages (day 7) was reduced when β1-integrins were blocked with mAb AIIB2 (Figure 7H and I).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 7H and I.

claims.claim: A β1-integrin-ERK pathway is responsible for stimulating epithelial proliferation.
claims.source: This implied that a β1-integrin-ERK pathway was responsible for stimulating epithelial proliferation.
claims.evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental results showing that blocking β1-integrins reduces ERK activation and proliferation.

claims.claim: Locoregional cell proliferation is a striking feature of MCF10A elongation in the experiments.
claims.source: These results lead us to conclude that a polarized collagen 1 matrix can promote epithelial elongation by stimulating locoregional cell proliferation. We infer this because (1) locoregional cell proliferation was a striking feature of MCF10A elongation in our experiments, whose loss was not compensated for by other morphogenetic processes.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on the experimental observations throughout the study.

claims.claim: The pattern of proliferation within aggregates is critically influenced by the polarized organization of the surrounding collagen 1 matrix.
claims.source: (2) The pattern of proliferation within aggregates was critically influenced by the polarized organization of the surrounding collagen 1 matrix.
claims.evidence: The claim is based on the experimental observations showing that collagen polarization affects proliferation patterns.

claims.claim: Collagen polarization and cell proliferation interact to guide epithelial elongation.
claims.source: Together, we suggest that these reveal an interplay between collagen polarization and cell proliferation that can guide epithelial elongation (Figure 8).
claims.evidence: The claim is a synthesis of the experimental findings presented in the study.

claims.claim: Inhibiting proliferation early in the culture process blocks branching morphogenesis in mouse mammary organoids.
claims.source: Elongation was reduced when mitomycin C and aphidicolin were added from the beginning of the assays, consistent with earlier evidence that inhibiting proliferation early in the culture process blocked branching morphogenesis in mouse mammary organoids (Ewald et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Ewald et al., 2008.

claims.claim: Elongation is compromised if proliferation is inhibited after the elongation process has begun, a later dependence that was not seen in organoids.
claims.source: We also found that elongation was compromised if proliferation was inhibited after the elongation process had begun, a later dependence that was not seen in organoids (Huebner et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and citation to Huebner et al., 2016.

claims.claim: Collagen 1 orientation induces mammary organoid branching.
claims.source: Similarly, collagen 1 orientation has been reported to induce mammary organoid branching (Brownfield et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Brownfield et al., 2013.

claims.claim: Increasing fibril alignment in acellular collagen gels increases fiber stiffness and decreases pore size.
claims.source: Increasing fibril alignment in acellular collagen gels was reported to increase fiber stiffness and decrease pore size (Riching et al., 2014; Taufalele et al., 2019), even in the absence of externally applied forces.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Riching et al., 2014 and Taufalele et al., 2019.

claims.claim: In single-cell cultures, aligned collagen fibers are associated with larger focal adhesions than non-aligned fibrils.
claims.source: Moreover, in single-cell cultures aligned collagen fibers were associated with larger focal adhesions than non-aligned fibrils (Doyle and Yamada, 2016).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Doyle and Yamada, 2016.

claims.claim: Integrins sense changes in matrix stiffness.
claims.source: This is consistent with the well-characterized role for integrins to sense changes in matrix stiffness (Giannone and Sheetz, 2006).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Giannone and Sheetz, 2006.

claims.claim: Cell migration is a key driver of branching morphogenesis.
claims.source: Cell migration is a key driver of branching morphogenesis (Gjorevski et al., 2015; Huebner et al., 2016), and earlier experiments reported that the application of external stretch to collagen-embedded aggregates could promote elongation through cell migration (Brownfield et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gjorevski et al., 2015, Huebner et al., 2016, and Brownfield et al., 2013.

claims.claim: The application of external stretch to collagen-embedded aggregates can promote elongation through cell migration.
claims.source: Cell migration is a key driver of branching morphogenesis (Gjorevski et al., 2015; Huebner et al., 2016), and earlier experiments reported that the application of external stretch to collagen-embedded aggregates could promote elongation through cell migration (Brownfield et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Brownfield et al., 2013.

claims.claim: Cells can orient their patterns of migration when collagen networks condense and form bundles in 2D systems.
claims.source: Studies in 2D systems have shown that cells can orient their patterns of migration when collagen networks condense and form bundles (Mohammed et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Mohammed et al., 2020 and Wang et al., 2018.

claims.claim: Anisotropic confinement can orient patterns of cell division in micropatterning experiments using 2D substrata.
claims.source: Micropatterning experiments using 2D substrata have shown that anisotropic confinement can orient patterns of cell division (Théry et al., 2005), potentially by orienting tensile stresses (Campinho et al., 2013; Legoff et al., 2013), as would also be predicted to accompany stiffer, condensed collagen bundles.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Théry et al., 2005, Campinho et al., 2013, and Legoff et al., 2013.

claims.claim: The basement membrane thins substantially and is remodeled in regions of epithelial elongation, such as the tips of mammary or salivary gland buds.
claims.source: However, earlier studies reported that the basement membrane thins substantially and is remodeled in regions of epithelial elongation, such as the tips of mammary or salivary gland buds (Harunaga et al., 2014; Silberstein and Daniel, 1982; Williams and Daniel, 1983), potentially allowing elongating regions of epithelia to engage with collagen 1.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Harunaga et al., 2014, Silberstein and Daniel, 1982, and Williams and Daniel, 1983.

claims.claim: Regional polarization of the collagen 1 matrix begins in response to anisotropies in force that aggregates exert upon their ECM via their integrin adhesions.
claims.source: In conclusion, we propose the following working model (Figure 8): regional polarization of the collagen 1 matrix begins in response to anisotropies in force that aggregates exert upon their ECM via their integrin adhesions (Figure 7A).
claims.evidence: The claim is part of the proposed working model based on the experimental findings.

claims.claim: Cell-based forces exerted through integrins can apply strain on collagen fibrils.
claims.source: Cell-based forces exerted through integrins can apply strain on collagen fibrils (Brownfield et al., 2013; Buchmann et al., 2021; Gjorevski et al., 2015; Hall et al., 2016) and, consistent with this, collagen reorganization in our experiments was compromised by inhibiting cellular contractility.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Brownfield et al., 2013, Buchmann et al., 2021, Gjorevski et al., 2015, and Hall et al., 2016, and experimental data.

claims.claim: Collagen polarization stimulates further cell proliferation in adjacent parts of the aggregate to sustain elongation.
claims.source: The consequent locoregional collagen polarization then stimulates further cell proliferation in the adjacent parts of the aggregate to sustain elongation.
claims.evidence: The claim is part of the proposed working model based on the experimental findings.

claims.claim: Polarized collagen networks can provide a structural memory of the initial axis of symmetry breaking, a relatively long-lived spatial cue that directs further elongation of epithelial anlagen.
claims.source: This would allow polarized collagen networks to effectively provide a structural memory of the initial axis of symmetry breaking, that is, a relatively long-lived spatial cue that directs further elongation of the epithelial anlagen.
claims.evidence: The claim is part of the proposed working model based on the experimental findings.

claims.claim: Branched tubules represent one of the archetypal modes of epithelial organization.
claims.source: Branched tubules represent one of the archetypal modes of epithelial organization (Iruela-Arispe and Beitel, 2013; Varner and Nelson, 2014).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Iruela-Arispe and Beitel, 2013 and Varner and Nelson, 2014.

claims.claim: In organs such as the mammary gland and lungs, networks of hollow epithelial tubes mediate the physiological exchange of gases, nutrients, and solutes between the body and its external environment.
claims.source: In organs such as the mammary gland and lungs, networks of hollow epithelial tubes mediate the physiological exchange of gases, nutrients, and solutes between the body and its external environment (Chung and Andrew, 2008).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Chung and Andrew, 2008.

claims.claim: Epithelial networks are established by a complex morphogenetic process where tubules grow outward from their precursors until they are instructed to branch, after which outgrowth continues until the network is completed.
claims.source: These definitive networks are established by a complex morphogenetic process, where tubules grow outward from their precursors until they are instructed to branch, after which outgrowth continues until the network is completed (Affolter et al., 2009; Andrew and Ewald, 2010).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Affolter et al., 2009 and Andrew and Ewald, 2010.

claims.claim: In the trachea, lumens appear early and accompany the growth of tubules.
claims.source: For example, in the trachea, lumens appear early and accompany the growth of tubules (Schottenfeld et al., 2010), whereas in the salivary and mammary glands tubules first begin as non-polarized cellular aggregates (or anlage), which then elongate as solid, multicellular cords before eventually forming lumens (Bastidas-Ponce et al., 2017; Nerger and Nelson, 2019; Tucker, 2007).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Schottenfeld et al., 2010.

claims.claim: In the salivary and mammary glands, tubules first begin as non-polarized cellular aggregates (or anlage), which then elongate as solid, multicellular cords before eventually forming lumens.
claims.source: For example, in the trachea, lumens appear early and accompany the growth of tubules (Schottenfeld et al., 2010), whereas in the salivary and mammary glands tubules first begin as non-polarized cellular aggregates (or anlage), which then elongate as solid, multicellular cords before eventually forming lumens (Bastidas-Ponce et al., 2017; Nerger and Nelson, 2019; Tucker, 2007).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bastidas-Ponce et al., 2017, Nerger and Nelson, 2019, and Tucker, 2007.

claims.claim: The decision to branch is a critical checkpoint controlled by developmental signals and cell-cell and cell-ECM interactions.
claims.source: The decision to branch is recognized to be a critical checkpoint that is controlled by developmental signals and cell-cell and cell-extracellular matrix (cell-ECM) interactions (Goodwin and Nelson, 2020).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Goodwin and Nelson, 2020.

claims.claim: The elongation of tubule precursors is a regulated process controlled by receptor tyrosine kinases and other signaling pathways.
claims.source: The elongation of tubule precursors is also thought to be a regulated process controlled by receptor tyrosine kinases and other signaling pathways (Costantini and Kopan, 2010; Gjorevski and Nelson, 2010; Sternlicht et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Costantini and Kopan, 2010, Gjorevski and Nelson, 2010, and Sternlicht et al., 2006.

claims.claim: Type 1 collagen is often the dominant form of collagen during epithelial tubulogenesis.
claims.source: One of the main components of ECM is collagen, particularly type 1 collagen (also called collagen 1), which is often the dominant form during epithelial tubulogenesis (Graham et al., 1988; Keely et al., 1995; Llacua et al., 2018; Nakanishi et al., 1986; Simon-Assmann et al., 1995).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Graham et al., 1988, Keely et al., 1995, Llacua et al., 2018, Nakanishi et al., 1986, and Simon-Assmann et al., 1995.

claims.claim: Fibrillar collagen helps scaffold other molecules, such as other ECM proteins and growth factors.
claims.source: Fibrillar collagen helps scaffold other molecules, such other ECM proteins and growth factors (Kanematsu et al., 2004; Wipff and Hinz, 2008).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kanematsu et al., 2004 and Wipff and Hinz, 2008.

claims.claim: Adhesion between cells and ECM allows the chemical and mechanical properties of the ECM to regulate cell signaling and gene regulation.
claims.source: Adhesion between cells and ECM allows the chemical and mechanical properties of the ECM to regulate cell signaling and gene regulation (Shi et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Shi et al., 2011.

claims.claim: Cell-ECM adhesions allow cell-based forces to reorganize the ECM.
claims.source: These cell-ECM adhesions also allow cell-based forces to reorganize the ECM. In particular, cells can rearrange collagen fibrils to influence cell migration (Buchmann et al., 2021; Gjorevski et al., 2015; Guo et al., 2012; Shi et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Buchmann et al., 2021, Gjorevski et al., 2015, Guo et al., 2012, and Shi et al., 2014.

claims.claim: Fibrillar components of the ECM, such as collagen 1, are relatively long-lived.
claims.source: Importantly, fibrillar components of the ECM, such as collagen 1, are relatively long-lived (Price and Spiro, 1977; Verzijl et al., 2000), making them attractive candidates to bridge time scales during the elongation process.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Price and Spiro, 1977 and Verzijl et al., 2000.

claims.claim: Rearrangement of collagen has been implicated in patterning epithelial branching.
claims.source: Indeed, rearrangement of collagen has been implicated in patterning epithelial branching (Brownfield et al., 2013; Guo et al., 2012; Harunaga et al., 2011; Ingman et al., 2006; Patel et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Brownfield et al., 2013, Guo et al., 2012, Harunaga et al., 2011, Ingman et al., 2006, and Patel et al., 2006.

results.result: MCF10A cells cultured in Matrigel form polarized aggregates with lumens, whereas cells in type 1 collagen gel form elongated, solid cords. When aggregates are transplanted from Matrigel into collagen gel, they spontaneously break symmetry and elongate into solid, cord-like structures.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C5 establish the experimental system and demonstrate that the ECM environment (Matrigel vs. collagen) determines aggregate morphology. The observations are supported by imaging data (Figures 1B, 2A, Video 1) and citations to prior work. The transplantation assay provides a controlled method to study symmetry breaking and elongation.

results.result: Cell proliferation is spatially heterogeneous during aggregate elongation, with Ki67-positive cells being approximately twofold more frequent in elongating regions (41.00% ± 4.55%) compared to non-elongating regions (18.86% ± 3.05%). This differential proliferation is established early, appearing at day 2 and preceding symmetry breaking at day 3.
results.evaluation: Claims C6-C10 demonstrate locoregional differences in proliferation using both Ki67 immunostaining and live-cell imaging of nuclear division. The quantitative data show statistically significant differences between elongating and non-elongating regions, and the temporal analysis establishes that increased proliferation precedes morphological changes. The data are internally consistent across multiple measurement approaches.

results.result: Cell proliferation is required for aggregate elongation. Treatment with mitomycin C or aphidicolin significantly reduces both proliferation (to 3.88% ± 1.18% and 11.54% ± 3.55%, respectively, vs. 26.63% ± 3.34% in controls at day 8) and elongation. Inhibiting proliferation after symmetry breaking (day 3) reduces elongation by approximately threefold, indicating that proliferation is required both for initiating and sustaining elongation.
results.evaluation: Claims C11-C15 establish causality through pharmacological inhibition experiments. The use of two independent inhibitors (mitomycin C and aphidicolin) strengthens the conclusion. The temporal manipulation (adding inhibitors at day 3) demonstrates that proliferation is required at multiple stages. The quantitative data show dose-dependent effects on both proliferation and elongation metrics.

results.result: Cells within elongating regions tend to divide along the axis of elongation, with the angle difference between cell division axis and principal axis being smaller in elongating areas compared to non-elongating areas.
results.evaluation: Claims C16-C17 demonstrate oriented cell division using live-cell imaging and quantitative angle measurements. The data show that cell division orientation correlates with aggregate elongation direction, suggesting a potential mechanism for directional growth. However, the contribution of oriented division versus increased proliferation rate to elongation is not fully resolved.

results.result: Cells are motile within aggregates, with identical migration speeds in elongating and non-elongating regions. However, cells in elongating areas show slightly greater track straightness and smaller track displacement angles relative to the elongation axis. Blocking proliferation reduces track straightness and increases displacement angle without affecting migration speed.
results.evaluation: Claims C18-C23 characterize cell migration using nuclear tracking. The data show that migration speed is not the primary driver of elongation, but directional persistence and alignment with the elongation axis differ between regions. The effect of proliferation inhibitors on migration parameters suggests coupling between proliferation and directed migration, though the mechanism is unclear.

results.result: Re-embedded aggregates lose laminin V expression over time but maintain fibronectin expression throughout the experiments without regional differences.
results.evaluation: Claims C24-C25 document changes in ECM protein expression during the transplantation process. The loss of laminin V is consistent with the transition from Matrigel to collagen environment. The uniform fibronectin expression suggests it is not a primary driver of regional differences in elongation. The data are descriptive and serve to characterize the experimental system.

results.result: Collagen 1 condenses around elongating aggregates, forming dense bands. Collagen coherency (bundling) increases with aggregate symmetry ratio and is greater in regions proximate to elongating parts compared to non-elongating parts. This increased coherency is evident early during symmetry breaking (first 3 days).
results.evaluation: Claims C26-C30 demonstrate that collagen reorganization accompanies aggregate elongation. The use of coherency as a quantitative measure of collagen bundling is appropriate, though the authors acknowledge limitations in visualizing individual fibrils. The correlation between coherency and elongation is established, and the temporal analysis shows this occurs early in the process. The data support a relationship between collagen organization and elongation.

results.result: Collagen bundling requires cell proliferation and cellular contractility. Coherency is reduced by mitomycin C, aphidicolin, blebbistatin, and Y27632, but not by the Rac1 inhibitor NSC23766.
results.evaluation: Claims C31-C33 establish that collagen reorganization depends on cell-generated forces. The use of multiple inhibitors targeting different pathways (proliferation, myosin, ROCK, Rac1) provides mechanistic insight. The lack of effect with NSC23766 suggests that Rac1-dependent processes (e.g., lamellipodia-driven migration) are not required for collagen bundling, consistent with the earlier finding that migration speed is not altered in elongating regions.

results.result: Collagen fibrils around elongating regions of aggregates are polarized and oriented with the principal axis of aggregate elongation. The angle difference between collagen polarity and aggregate elongation is significantly smaller around elongating regions than non-elongating regions.
results.evaluation: Claims C34-C36 demonstrate that collagen not only bundles but also becomes oriented during elongation. The quantitative analysis of fibril orientation relative to the aggregate axis is rigorous. This establishes that collagen organization is anisotropic around elongating aggregates, which is critical for the subsequent stretch experiments.

results.result: External mechanical stretch can polarize collagen fibrils, making them more coherent and oriented in the direction of stretch. This polarization can be preserved for at least 7 days by re-embedding stretched gels in a larger collagen gel, but reverts to isotropic organization if gels are allowed to float.
results.evaluation: Claims C37-C39 establish a method to manipulate collagen organization independently of cell-generated forces. The use of second harmonic imaging provides direct visualization of collagen structure. The ability to preserve or reverse polarization by re-embedding or floating provides experimental control over collagen organization, which is essential for testing causality.

results.result: Stretch-induced collagen polarization accelerates aggregate elongation without causing immediate deformation during stretch. Symmetry breaking occurs earlier in stretch-polarized gels (35.14 ± 3.28 hr) compared to controls (68.40 ± 5.88 hr), and aggregates elongate preferentially along the stretch axis with greater symmetry ratios. Collagen reorganization is preserved in stretch-polarized gels and oriented with the original stretch direction.
results.evaluation: Claims C40-C46 demonstrate that collagen polarization is sufficient to direct aggregate elongation. The temporal separation between stretch application and elongation onset argues against direct mechanical effects on cells. The preferential orientation along the stretch axis and the preservation of collagen organization provide strong evidence that cells are responding to the polarized collagen matrix. The lack of effect on fibronectin deposition (C46) suggests specificity for collagen.

results.result: The stimulatory effect of stretch on elongation is lost when collagen polarization is reversed by floating gels. Cell-based forces cannot overcome external forces that cause collagen depolarization.
results.evaluation: Claims C47-C48 provide critical controls showing that the effect of stretch depends on sustained collagen polarization rather than transient mechanical stimulation of cells. The inability of cell forces to maintain polarization when gels are floated demonstrates the dominance of external mechanical constraints in this system. This strengthens the conclusion that collagen organization, not cell memory of stretch, drives elongation.

results.result: Stretch-induced collagen polarization stimulates cell proliferation, with Ki67-positive cells appearing earlier (day 1) and at higher proportions throughout culture compared to unstretched gels. This enhanced proliferation mediates the accelerated elongation, as both length and symmetry ratio are reduced by mitomycin C and aphidicolin. The proliferative response requires sustained collagen polarization, as it is lost when gels are floated.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C54 establish the mechanism by which collagen polarization promotes elongation: by stimulating cell proliferation. The temporal analysis shows proliferation increases before morphological changes, consistent with a causal relationship. The requirement for sustained polarization (C54) links collagen organization to the proliferative response. The inhibitor experiments confirm that proliferation mediates the effect of stretch on elongation.

results.result: ERK is preferentially activated in elongating regions of aggregates, particularly in cells at the surface in contact with collagen. No changes in nuclear Yap1 localization are detected, suggesting the Hippo pathway is not activated.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-C57 identify ERK as a candidate signaling pathway linking collagen organization to proliferation. The use of the ERK/KTR biosensor provides spatial resolution of pathway activity. The enrichment at the cell-collagen interface is consistent with integrin-mediated signaling. The negative result for Yap1 (C57) helps rule out alternative pathways, though the analysis is limited to nuclear localization and may not capture all aspects of Hippo signaling.

results.result: The ERK inhibitor FR180204 reduces cell proliferation in response to stretch polarization and decreases both the proportion of aggregates that elongate and the length and asymmetry of those that do elongate. ERK1/2 is critical for collagen polarization to stimulate cell proliferation and aggregate elongation.
results.evaluation: Claims C58-C60 establish ERK as a key mediator of the collagen-proliferation-elongation axis. The pharmacological inhibition experiments show dose-dependent effects on proliferation and elongation. However, the specificity of FR180204 for ERK vs. other kinases is not fully validated, and off-target effects cannot be ruled out. Additional validation with genetic approaches or alternative inhibitors would strengthen the conclusion.

results.result: MCF10A cells express α2β1-integrin. The β1-integrin blocking antibody AIIB2 inhibits stretch-induced proliferation and elongation. After 3 days, 49.19% ± 1.61% of control aggregates elongate vs. 17.86% ± 4.78% with AIIB2. AIIB2-treated aggregates that eventually elongate remain shorter and less asymmetric. AIIB2 reduces ERK activation at both early (day 2) and late (day 7) stages, indicating a β1-integrin-ERK pathway stimulates proliferation.
results.evaluation: Claims C61-C66 identify β1-integrin as the receptor linking collagen polarization to ERK activation and proliferation. The expression data (C61) confirm the presence of collagen-binding integrins. The AIIB2 blocking experiments show dose-dependent effects on proliferation, elongation, and ERK activation. The temporal analysis (C65) demonstrates sustained requirement for integrin signaling. However, AIIB2 blocks all β1-integrins, not just α2β1, so the specific collagen receptor is not definitively identified.

results.result: A polarized collagen 1 matrix promotes epithelial elongation by stimulating locoregional cell proliferation. The pattern of proliferation within aggregates is critically influenced by the polarized organization of the surrounding collagen matrix. Collagen polarization and cell proliferation interact to guide epithelial elongation.
results.evaluation: Claims C67-C69 synthesize the major findings into a coherent model. The conclusion is well-supported by the experimental data showing: (1) locoregional proliferation accompanies elongation, (2) proliferation is required for elongation, (3) collagen polarization stimulates proliferation, and (4) the β1-integrin-ERK pathway mediates this response. The interplay between cell-generated forces (which polarize collagen) and collagen-stimulated proliferation (which sustains elongation) is a key insight.

results.result: In the MCF10A system, elongation is compromised when proliferation is inhibited either early or after elongation has begun. This differs from mouse mammary organoids where later inhibition of proliferation does not affect elongation.
results.evaluation: Claims C70-C71 compare the current findings to prior work on organoids. The citations support the comparison, and the experimental data (C14) demonstrate the sustained requirement for proliferation in the MCF10A system. This highlights potential differences between model systems and suggests that the relative contributions of proliferation vs. other processes (e.g., migration) may vary.

results.result: Prior work has shown that collagen orientation induces mammary organoid branching, that aligned collagen fibers have increased stiffness and decreased pore size, that aligned fibers are associated with larger focal adhesions, and that integrins sense matrix stiffness.
results.evaluation: Claims C72-C75 cite relevant prior work to contextualize the findings. The citations are appropriate and support the discussion of potential mechanisms by which cells might sense collagen polarization (e.g., through changes in stiffness or focal adhesion size). These are background claims that help interpret the results.

results.result: Prior work has established that cell migration is a key driver of branching morphogenesis, that external stretch can promote elongation through migration, that cells can orient migration in response to collagen bundling in 2D, and that anisotropic confinement can orient cell division.
results.evaluation: Claims C76-C79 cite relevant prior work on migration and division orientation. The citations are appropriate and help contextualize the current findings on cell behavior during elongation. The discussion acknowledges that migration and oriented division may contribute to elongation alongside proliferation, though the current data suggest proliferation is the primary driver in this system.

results.result: Prior studies have shown that the basement membrane thins and is remodeled in regions of epithelial elongation, potentially allowing epithelia to engage with collagen 1.
results.evaluation: Claim C80 cites relevant prior work to address a potential limitation of the model: the absence of a basement membrane in the collagen gel system. The citations support the notion that basement membrane remodeling occurs during elongation in vivo, which could allow collagen-epithelial interactions. This is a reasonable discussion point, though direct evidence for such interactions in vivo is not provided.

results.result: The authors propose a working model where: (1) regional collagen polarization begins in response to anisotropic cell-generated forces via integrin adhesions, (2) cell forces can apply strain on collagen fibrils, (3) collagen polarization stimulates further proliferation to sustain elongation, and (4) polarized collagen provides a structural memory of the initial symmetry-breaking axis.
results.evaluation: Claims C81-C84 present the proposed model integrating the experimental findings. The model is well-supported by the data: collagen reorganization depends on cell contractility (C31-C32), collagen polarization stimulates proliferation (C50-C54), and collagen organization is long-lived (C38). The concept of 'structural memory' (C84) is speculative but reasonable given the stability of collagen networks. The model provides a coherent framework for understanding the results.

results.result: The introduction provides background on epithelial tubulogenesis, the role of ECM and collagen, and the regulation of branching and elongation, citing relevant prior work.
results.evaluation: Claims C85-C97 are background statements from the introduction that cite appropriate prior work. These establish the biological context and rationale for the study. The citations appear accurate and relevant. These are not experimental results but provide necessary context.
